messages:
lee: quick note from the perf run this morning: host ingress 95th jumped ~45ms after last night's preparse + kernel-select tweak

noah: ugh. short chat tail or long-context?

lee: short chats, typical <80 tokens. p50 steady, p95 up. flame shows tokenizer writev fragmentation + syscall spikes to sendmsg

maria: did we change MSG_MORE handling anywhere? small writes + no MSG_MORE will force TCP flushes

alex: kernel selector PR favored the tiny-kernel for mixed-shape batches, that reduced compute time but may alter timing of when we call writev

lee: exact flame (trimmed):
```
host_ingress_parse  40%  tokenizer:emit_frame
syscall:sendmsg     30%  grpc::Writev
kvcache_ops         15%  kv.put/kick
others              15%
```

sara: kv.put spike? we shouldn't be inserting prefixes in host path. Are preparse control tokens creating transient keys?

lee: yeah, we saw many tiny put ops when parser hits a control token and flushes a partial prefix to kvcache for resume semantics

noah: so two orthogonal regressions: early flush -> more kv churn, and kernel selector timing -> smaller microbatches leading to more per-request socket writes

alex: solution candidates:
- revert early prefix flush in preparse (safe short-term)
- reintroduce MSG_MORE in tokenizer sink so kernel-level writev coalesces records
- change kernel selector: if expected_coalesced_batch >=2 and seq_len<64 prefer default kernel (keeps batching alignment)
- add autobatcher adaptive hold: when arrival_rate > X, wait up to Y ms to try coalesce

maria: adaptive hold sounds risky for p50, but we can make it conditional: only when estimated tokenization emit cost is < C cycles and client not realtime flag

lee: also saw HTTP2 small-frame floods, WINDOW_UPDATE spikes. likely TLS record packing + writev fragmentation. restoring MSG_MORE should help there too

sara: I'll add eviction telemetry per-prefix and a short TTL for parser-inserted entries to limit GC pressure

noah: can we run a quick canary after reverting the preparse flush + MSG_MORE? two-phase: revert on canary, then kernel-selector autobatch tweak if canary looks good

lee: heading to put up the revert PR now. I'll include perf link: http://perf.internal/runs/612345

ops-bot: deploy requested by lee to canary-cluster-3 queued (id: dpl-612345) :package:

alex: i'll draft kernel-selector change and autobatcher feature flag so we can A/B easily

maria: if canary looks fine, plan a 3h soak with short-chat profile (ramp 200->1200 qps) and capture tcpdump + flame. also collect kv.put_rate, kv.hit_rate, writev_count per-second

lee: agreed. assigning tasks in the PR. thanks team. :rocket:
